memory_candidates.content: When a Gate 20 (orchestrator context budget) per-file ceiling fails, check whether the overage is a genuine new-mechanism cost (not restatable bloat) before bumping the ceiling. First look for a near-duplicate of an existing documented bash idiom elsewhere in the SAME file (e.g. a second bounded-wait/nohup/pid-capture/kill-0 block) and collapse it to a one-paragraph pointer substituting variable/script names into the first occurrence, rather than restating the whole block. Only after exhausting this kind of compaction does a reviewed, dated ceiling move (round the measured value up to the next 500 B) become the sanctioned path -- orchestrator-context-budget.json's own derivation history for skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md documents this exact pattern repeatedly.

A full verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh gate run executed while sibling /orchestrate tasks are concurrently dispatched in the same repo will surface genuine cross-task noise, not just hypothetical risk: observed live, a sibling task's own handoff-file write during a gate suite's run window tripped an unrelated suite's own contamination guard (a baseline-vs-final git-status diff of the real specs/ tree). When investigating a Gate 8 failure under known concurrent batch execution, diff the suite's own before/after repo-state snapshot (if it captures one) before assuming the failure is a real regression -- a single-line diff naming a sibling task's own artifact path is strong evidence of cross-task noise, not a defect in the subject script.
